prompt.context: Two technology firms within the audio-visual tech industry have decided to join forces. Their market — manufacturing of hardware components for audio-visual transmission — has been declining at a 14% rate, and this has affected their profitability, jeopardizing their future operations. Both of their CEOs have agreed on contracting a consulting firm to help them navigate the process.
prompt.question: Your job is to size the potential synergies that the operation may yield for the NewCo in the future.

clarifying_info.q: What does the audio-visual hardware market look like?
clarifying_info.a: Show Exhibit 1 — the industry insights exhibit.

clarifying_info.q: What segments do the companies serve?
clarifying_info.a: The companies work on a per-project basis, mainly for the hospitality segment (75% of their revenue).

clarifying_info.q: What do the companies actually do / what is their scope of operations?
clarifying_info.a: Their operations are limited to the manufacturing and assembly of hardware components; installation is done by a third party.
They are not based in the same country — one is in France and the other in Poland.

clarifying_info.q: Are the two companies of similar size and operations?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, they are both of similar size and have similar operations.

clarifying_info.q: How many plants do the companies have?
clarifying_info.a: The French company owns two plants (one in Southern France and one near Paris); the Polish company owns one bigger plant near Warsaw.
The objective is to improve their common profitability by 10% of the aggregated revenues.

exhibits.title: Industry Insights — HW Transmission Market
exhibits.shows: EU Total Accessible Market size in M€ for 2018, 2019, and 2020, plus a table of main competitors showing last-year revenue (M€) and 3-year CAGR. Also shows three product categories: Reception (Antennas, Encoders & Converters), Transmission (Wiring for different signals and network devices), and Terminals (End-user devices such as Smart TVs, Tablets, computers). A note states 80% of TAM depends on hospitality purchases and that hotels have been moving to software services.

exhibits.title: Revenues FY20 — French and Polish Companies
exhibits.shows: P&L summary for each company in FY2020 (all numbers in M€), broken down into Revenues, Variable Costs (Raw Materials, Transportation, Energy), Fixed Costs (Production/Salaries, R&D, Sales and Administration), and Operational Profit. Additional info states variable costs have been stable for 10 years and are not expected to change, and fixed costs have been increasing slowly with no hiring or firing for the last 6 years.

framework: Sales Synergies: identify revenue upside from cross-selling new products, accessing new geographies (France/Poland client bases), and gaining new clients previously exclusive to each company
Cost Synergies — Raw Materials: assess purchasing efficiency differences between companies; consider volume-based renegotiation or switching to the more efficient supplier
Cost Synergies — Direct Labour / Production: evaluate potential to consolidate manufacturing into the more cost-efficient location (Poland); quantify wage differential
Cost Synergies — R&D: identify duplication of R&D functions; consolidate into the more productive department (Poland) while eliminating duplicated spend
Cost Synergies — Sales & Administration: identify overlap in selling and administrative functions; centralize shared services
Other Considerations — Risks & Feasibility: assess risks to synergy consecution (cannibalization, legal/regulatory, reputational, liquidity) and feasibility of the merger action plan

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 1, what observations can you make about the industry and the rationale for this M&A?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note: (1) Overall market TAM declined from 800 to 660 M€ over 3 years = -17.5% cumulative decline. (2) Clients are switching from hardware to software services; Swedish competitor declined less because it acquired a software firm. (3) The combined NewCo (75+80 = 155 M€) would become the largest player in the market. (4) The Polish company has a better financial trajectory (lesser revenue decline). (5) Heavy client concentration in hospitality is a structural risk. (6) The M&A is likely driven by survival and synergy capture in a declining market.

steps: Combined NewCo revenue: 75 + 80 = 155 M€ (largest in market)
math.answer: Market declined ~17.5% over 3 years; NewCo becomes market leader at 155 M€

questions.prompt: Please structure your approach to sizing the synergies from this merger.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify two main sources: (1) Sales synergies — cross-selling, new geographies, new clients; (2) Cost synergies — raw materials purchasing, direct labour/production, R&D, sales & administration. A strong candidate adds a third bucket for risks and feasibility. The structure should be MECE and linked back to the P&L lines visible in Exhibit 2.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate the potential cost synergies from the merger. Consider a 70% consecution rate for target synergies.
questions.guidance: Candidate should work through each cost line: (1) Sales synergies = 0 (interviewer instructs candidate to assume zero given uncertainty and cannibalization risk). (2) Raw Materials: apply Polish purchasing ratio to French revenues to find potential saving. (3) Production: apply Polish salary ratio to French revenues to find saving from shifting production to Poland. (4) R&D: French R&D is fully duplicated; eliminate it and retain Polish budget. (5) S&A: partial overlap, estimate 2-3 M€. Apply 70% consecution. Separately identify one-off costs: termination costs of -10 M€ and plant sale proceeds of +2 M€.

math.setup: For each cost line, apply the more efficient company's ratio to the less efficient company's revenue base, then multiply total potential synergy by 70% consecution rate.
steps: Raw Materials synergy: French raw materials cost - (French revenue × Polish raw materials ratio) = 9 - (70 × 9.5/85) = 9 - 7.824 = 1.18 M€
Production synergy: French salaries - (French revenue × Polish salary ratio) = 42 - (70 × 33.5/85) = 42 - 27.59 = 14.41 M€
R&D synergy: eliminate French R&D entirely, retain Polish: 10 M€
Sales & Administration synergy: estimated overlap ~2.5 M€ (range 2-3 M€)
Target recurrent saving (70% consecution): 28.09 × 0.7 = 19.66 M€ ≈ 20 M€
One-off items: plant sale proceeds +2 M€, termination costs -10 M€, net one-off = -8 M€
math.answer: Target recurrent synergy ≈ 19.66 M€ (~20 M€); Year-0 one-off net loss of -8 M€

questions.prompt: What are the key risks that could prevent the NewCo from realising these synergies and threaten future profitability?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure risks by P&L line (revenues, variable costs, fixed costs). Strong answer references specific risks tied to this case (French labour law, production relocation difficulty) and proposes mitigation. Covering all three buckets in a structured way is a plus.

brainstorming.prompt: Elaborate on the risks associated with the NewCo's synergy implementation and future operations.

categories.name: Revenue risks
ideas: Competitive price war as market declines
Failure in consolidated R&D process leading to product obsolescence
Harming existing client relationships during integration
Cannibalization of sales between the two legacy brands

categories.name: Variable cost risks
ideas: Increase in price of raw material components
Decline in bargaining power against suppliers if current providers go bankrupt
Increase in energy and utility prices
Supply chain disruption from consolidating to fewer suppliers

categories.name: Fixed cost risks
ideas: Moving production from France to Poland may not be feasible due to government pressure or legal procedures
Employee dismissal may harm the company's reputation in the French market
Loss of R&D capability if key French R&D staff are not retained
Integration costs (IT, processes, culture) exceeding projections
Regulatory/antitrust scrutiny from creating the largest player in the market

recommendation: The merger has a target recurrent synergy potential of approximately 20 M€ per year (calculated at a 70% consecution rate on a 28 M€ gross potential)
The primary value drivers are Production/Labour (~14 M€ gross) and R&D consolidation (~10 M€ gross), both driven by shifting operations to the more cost-efficient Polish entity
In Year 0 the NewCo will incur a net one-off loss of approximately -8 M€ (termination costs of -10 M€ partially offset by French plant sale proceeds of +2 M€)
The 20 M€ annual synergy represents approximately 13% of combined revenues (155 M€), exceeding the stated 10% profitability improvement target
risks: French employment laws and government pressure may complicate or delay production relocation, raising actual one-off costs
Revenue cannibalization between the two legacy customer bases could erode sales synergies
Consolidation of R&D in Poland risks losing key French technical talent and slowing innovation
next_steps: Conduct detailed legal and HR due diligence on French plant closure and workforce reduction feasibility
Develop a phased integration roadmap with clear milestones for production transfer and R&D consolidation
Establish a change management and communication plan to protect client relationships and employee morale in France
